Implement state-driven guidance for the JusPrin project chat on a branch cut from local `jusprin-newui` (14 commits ahead of origin, not pushed; do not push). Report, untracked at your worktree root as `state-guidance-report.md`, in four parts: problem, what changed, tests and results, remaining issues; plain English for someone who did not see this session; never commit the report.

## Why

The project chat's system prompt (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`, 2,741 bytes, five sections) was reduced to principles on 2026-10-15. Kenneth's goal is an agent that answers every kind of request naturally (questions with or without a model, troubleshooting, import-slice-print) yet takes the right steps in the journeys that matter, above all: check the filament and process presets as soon as the purpose and the model are understood, and look at the model to tell what it is. Published practice (Anthropic's Agent Skills write-up, Replit's decision-time guidance, Pydantic's system reminders, Anthropic's "Writing tools for agents") agrees that standing rule lists fade and lose to the model's priors, while a short instruction supplied by the harness at the moment its situation arises, placed last in the request, works better; and that a tool's result should say what is now true and what has not yet been checked. Kenneth approved doing both of the following.

## A. Show the model the plate when a file opens

Today, when a file opens, `AgentHost::on_file_loaded` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp` about line 1318) appends a note message carrying the load report, and the model's next request gets `fileReportInstructions.ts` as a developer item (about line 2112). The model sees no picture unless it calls `view_render`. Change: attach the active plate's iso render to that file-open turn so the model sees the object without a tool call. Reuse the offscreen render `view_render` uses (`Workspace::render_view`, called from `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp` about line 1288); images already reach the model as `input_image` parts (`OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp` lines about 219 and 278). Decide whether the picture is stored with the message or rendered when the request is built; keep it out of the replayed history after that turn, because history is trimmed by a 64 KiB budget and a picture on every later request would be waste. Do not render when the project has no printable object. Widen `view_render`'s description in `ToolRegistry.cpp` (about line 1151) so it also serves to tell what an object is when its name does not say. Mention the picture in `fileReportInstructions.ts` in one sentence, deleting at least as much text as you add there.

## B. Notes and results that name what is unchecked

1. File just opened, nothing recorded about its purpose: on that same turn, one or two sentences saying that nothing is recorded about what this print is for, that the picture is the plate as loaded, and that the filament and process presets should be checked against what it is once that is known. Fold this into the file-open turn's existing developer text rather than adding a second item if that is simpler.
2. Intent just recorded: make `intent_update`'s tool result name the current printer, filament and process presets and the active plate's type as not yet checked against the recorded purpose (the host already treats `intent_update` specially around `AgentHost.cpp` line 624, `remember_setup_intent`). This is the tool-result channel; it needs no note.
3. Candidates, add only if something is missing: a slice that finished with warnings; a print issue clicked (these already arrive as `slice_report`'s result and the `<print_issue>` block). Judge and say why you did or did not add anything.

Rules for notes: never stored in the conversation document; the last item of the request; the same bytes for the same state so the prompt cache is not disturbed; the whole set stays a few sentences. On where the text lives: `agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md` says the text the model reads belongs on the Agent page, as `project_instructions` and `file_report_instructions` do, while text assembled from app state (the omission note, the workspace block) is built in C++. Follow that split and say in the report which side each new text is on and why.

Rule lives once: if a note or a result now covers a sentence of the prompt's Preparing section, delete that sentence, and the prompt's byte count must not go up. Never write "approve", "authorize", "confirm before" or "ask the user then call again" anywhere; tool-call approval was removed on 2026-10-07.

## C. Keep the eval in step

`tests/project_prompt` replays requests recorded from the app and asks the model for one step; a case must name the prompt sentence or note it tests and never runs past its first response. Re-record `requests.json` with the shell harness's `--project-prompt-requests` after your change (the recorder waits for OrcaSlicer's scheduled update, selects a per-conversation `plateType`, and points the version check at a closed port; all on the branch already). Add one first-step case at the point right after `intent_update`'s new result, expecting a read of the effective settings, `presets_list` or `printer_setup_preview`, and failing on `slice_start` or a readiness claim. The file-note case will now carry a picture; check it still renders. In the main checkout the cases `petg-restated` and `petg-restated-after-read` were deleted today, uncommitted (their step removed from `script.json`'s `prepare` conversation, their classes removed from `run_prompt_tests.py`, their `test_steps.py` use retargeted to `file-note-not-instructions`); make the identical deletion before you re-record so the two trees agree.

Do not run a live model batch without Kenneth's approval: put the proposed batch (cases, runs, estimated tokens) in the report instead. Credentials for a later run live in `~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`; never print them.

## D. Tests and build

Run `agent_bridge_tests` (cmake at `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake`, target `agent_bridge_tests`, config RelWithDebInfo; nohup long builds and watch the log; `cd` into your worktree in every Bash call), the AgentUI vitest suite (build `jusprin_web` after page edits), `workspace_contract_tests`, the shell harness default scenario, and `python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py` plus `run_prompt_tests.py --render-only`. New behaviour gets a test that fails without the change. Report line counts added and removed. Commit code and tests on your branch with plain commit messages and no attribution lines; do not commit docs or reports.
I'll start by orienting in the worktree: checking which branch I'm on versus local `jusprin-newui`, then reading the files the task names.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

Branch `claude/project-prompt-harness` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/project-prompt-harness`), commit 70366449ae on jusprin-newui 336facf825. Not pushed. Baseline run 2026-10-15 at Kenneth's request (29df4b87f8): today's prompt 6b4b8b6188, 3 runs: 39/54 pass, 4 fail, 11 unobserved; 599,356 input tokens (459,776 cached), 9,784 output, 3 judge calls. The model often reads before replying, so first-person and reply-in-german observed no reply (0 pass, 3 unobserved each); answer-from-context 0/3 (calls workspace_inspect).

Design that differs from the 2026-10-15 handover, and why:
- Requests are recorded whole by a new shell harness mode, `--project-prompt-requests <script.json> <out.json>`: the project chat's real OpenAIResponsesAgent with a transport that holds each request; the scenario answers with scripted model outputs, so tools run for real and the app builds every request. `--manual-mcp` could not do it: in-turn tool results carry a `workspace` block (AgentHost::continue_after_tool, `context_json`) that MCP results never contain, and MCP rewrites stale errors to `stale_workspace` (in-app also says `stale_workspace` now).
- Case 16 uses the printer start G-code (22 KB) because presets_list pages at 25 (~1.5 KB) and every other read here stays under 4 KB: the 16 KiB omission note never fires for them.
- Cases 7/8 use initial_layer_print_height 0.5: a hand-typed layer_height above max_layer_height (0.28) is reset by an Orca dialog.
- Case 18's 3MF is written by the recorder (model_info->description + export_3mf); a PrusaSlicer 3MF loads geometry only and drops the description.

App problems found while recording (reported, not fixed): printer_setup_preview says valid/no mismatch for Bambu PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate, then Orca refuses to slice; slice_start wait:true on that plate stays running (up to 15 min by the code) instead of failing.

**Why:** the next session runs Kenneth's batch or re-records after tool changes.
**How to apply:** re-record with the harness command in tests/project_prompt/README.md after tool/result changes; batch needs Kenneth's approval and the rewritten prompt. Related: [[project-prompt-harness-critique]], [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]], [[manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe]].

**2026-10-15 later: Kenneth reversed the strict one-step rule for reads** (a9ffaf06e6): a read the case doesn't decide on is answered from real results the recorder captured at that point (workspace_inspect, slice_report, printer_list, settings_get of 32 keys for print + first object), max 3 per run; changes/judged calls still end the run. He wants flexibility, not exact-path expectations ("LMs are not deterministic"). First single run: 7 of 23 ended "no recorded answer" (settings_search, filament keys, legacy keys like fill_density, object_analyze, string targets) — answer coverage is the open weakness.

**Baseline with answered reads (f911bad664, 2026-10-15):** 23 cases x 3 on 6b4b8b6188, recording 80eddcbe9e (27 answers/point, requests.json ~4 MB): 47/69 pass, 8 fail, 14 unobserved; 1,256,920 input tokens (925,696 cached). Unobserved = string-JSON targets (app refuses), free-worded settings_search, object_analyze, unrecorded keys. Older 39/54 baseline not comparable.

**346a811aad (2026-10-15):** recording adds object_analyze per active-plate object (eachObject), 49 word-order-free settings_search queries, a few more names; workspace block stored once per point (sharedWorkspace) and reinserted byte-exact by the runner. requests.json ~6.7 MB (searches ~4.3 MB). 10 of the baseline's 14 unanswered reads now covered (offline replay); the 4 left are string-JSON targets. Not yet run live on this recording.

**708735c9ab:** reran the 7 cases with unanswered reads on 346a811aad (21 runs, 602,761 input tokens); baseline now 52/69 pass, 10 fail, 7 unobserved (rows marked by recording). Remaining misses: single setting names (slow_down_layers, bridge_no_support, filament_ramming_parameters), search wordings, string targets. The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the file the person just opened. They have asked for nothing yet, so this message reports and offers, from the report alone.

The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what arrived and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. uiLanguage is the app's interface language, supplied even when there are no notices.

Write one useful message for someone new to 3D printing. Lead with the most consequential unresolved issue. Explain what it means for this print in everyday language. When an issue remains, end with one specific next step I can help with, phrased as one question or offer; do not give a menu of alternatives. Briefly explain an unfamiliar term when the person needs it to understand the consequence. Explain where a warning came from when the report shows it: what the file contains, what I noticed while loading it, whether its settings were applied, and what still needs checking. | Notice or event you may encounter | Importance and explanation for the person |
| --- | --- |

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the 28 project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. It is run against the prompt before an edit and after it, and the
counts compared. The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge.

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

A call with arguments the registry would refuse is never answered either; it
is the step, reported beside it, and refusals are the C++ tests' business.
A run's report names every call of the response it ended on. `test_steps.py`
checks these rules offline against written model outputs, with no key and
nothing sent (`python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`).

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
`answers` list names:

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`;
- `object_analyze` for every object on every plate with every `include`
  but `measure`, given for that object and session whatever it included;
  never with `measure` or `candidates`;
- every setting, read with `settings_get`: of the print, of every object on
  every plate, of the selected filament and of the printer (355, 275 each,
  126 and 171 in the current recording). The keys come from the app itself:
  an empty `settings_search` query lists every setting of a scope, page by
  page. The filament's and printer's keys are also read under the print
  scope, and the print-wide settings under each object's scope, so a name
  asked for under the wrong scope gets the app's own answer, and so are three hand-kept lists of names the model takes from
  other slicers or invents (`fill_density`, `perimeters`,
  `initial_layer_height`...). A model's `settings_get` is answered with
  exactly the keys it asked for, in its order, each taken from those reads
  of the same scope and target, around the rest of the first such result;
- `settings_search` for 49 queries, given when the scope, target and
  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed; never for `changedOnly`. A search
  result is the app's ranking for that query, so a wording not recorded has
  no answer.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Recording all 24
points takes under three minutes. To keep `requests.json` small (about
3 MB), the recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide
(`settingItems`), and each point's workspace block once when a result
repeats it exactly (`sharedWorkspace`); the runner and the schema test put
both back byte for byte. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a
string of JSON (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 38
distinct reads that ended runs unobserved in the runs of 2026-10-15, 26 are
now recorded; the other 12 are string targets, `changedOnly` searches,
search wordings not recorded, and setting names that do not exist in
OrcaSlicer.

This is not the design that failed on 2026-10-10. That one answered every
call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's

  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:

  ```bash
  build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
      --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json tests/project_prompt/requests.json
  ```

  chat's real OpenAI adapter, but the adapter's requests go nowhere: each is
  answered with the next model output the script gives. The tools run for

  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and

  the calls were written. Each answer carries the action id and workspace

# State-driven guidance for the project chat

Branch `claude/state-guidance`, cut from local `jusprin-newui` at 77115d05b3, three commits on top (17112e7e71, 553916458f, e3bf144b00). Not pushed. This file is untracked and stays so.

## 1. The problem

The project chat's assistant is told everything it should do in one standing system prompt of five sections (2,741 bytes before this change). Two things matter most in Kenneth's view of a good print journey: as soon as the purpose of a print and the model itself are understood, the assistant should check the filament and process presets against them; and when a model's name does not say what it is, the assistant should look at it. The standing prompt asked for both in general terms. Published practice on agent prompting says that general rules fade as a chat grows and lose to the model's habits, while a short instruction given by the app at the exact moment its situation arises, placed last in the request, is followed; and that a tool's result should say what is now true and what has not yet been checked.

Two moments in the app matched that pattern and had nothing in place:

- When a person opens a file, the assistant's first message was written from a text report alone. It saw no picture of what had arrived unless it spent a tool call on `view_render`, and nothing told it that the print's purpose was still unknown.
- When the assistant records what a print is for with `intent_update`, the tool's result said only that the record was written. Nothing in that result said that the printer, filament, process and plate in force had been chosen before that purpose existed and had not been checked against it.

## 2. What changed

### A. The model sees the plate when a file opens

The first request after a file opens now carries a picture of the active plate. It is the same offscreen render `view_render` gives (the iso view, 1024 by 768, printable objects without the bed), produced by the host when it builds that one request, and sent as the last part of the turn's user message as an image input. No picture is rendered when the plate has no printable object (Orca's own count of printable objects on the active plate, or, where that count is not available, any object on the plate).

I chose to render when the request is built rather than store the picture with the message. Stored, it would sit as base64 inside the project's saved chat document and need removing from later requests by hand; built on demand, it is never in the document, a retried attempt renders again, and no later turn can carry it, which keeps it out of the replayed history that the 64 KiB budget trims. The turn starts in the same event-loop pass that delivers the load report, so the picture is the plate as loaded.

Related text changes: the `view_render` description now also offers the picture "to tell what an object is when its name does not say" (so `project_tools.json`, the eval's copy of the tool list, was regenerated); `fileReportInstructions.ts` gained one sentence telling the assistant what to do with the picture when one is present (115 bytes) and lost two sentences the rest of the text already covered (184 bytes).

### B. Saying what is unchecked, at the moment it matters

**B1. The file-open turn's note.** The same request ends with a developer item, built by the host from the state at that moment: "Nothing is recorded yet about what this print is for. The picture is the plate as loaded. Once its purpose is known, check the filament and process presets against that purpose." The middle sentence is left out when no picture was rendered; the whole item is left out when a purpose is already recorded for the conversation. It is never stored. The same state always produces the same bytes, and it is the last item of the request, so the request's cached opening is untouched.

I did not fold it into the existing file-report developer item. That item is the first item of the request, placed before the history, and the rule for notes is that they come last; folding would have meant either moving the 6.8 KB file-report text to the end or putting the note first. A separate trailing item was simpler and keeps the rule.

**B2. `intent_update`'s result.** The result now ends with `unchecked`, a sentence built from the live workspace: "Not yet checked against the recorded purpose: printer preset Bambu Lab X1 Carbon 0.4 nozzle, filament preset Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C, process preset 0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C, plate type Smooth Cool Plate." (that is the sentence the recorder captured from the real app). Parts the workspace cannot name are left out; the output schema requires the field. This is the tool-result channel, so it needs no note.

**B3. Candidates not added.** A slice that finished with warnings: `slice_start`'s result says the run finished, its description sends the model to `slice_report`, the Preparing section says to check `slice_report` before calling a print ready, and the `after-slice` eval case passed 3 of 3 on the current prompt. A print issue clicked: the `<print_issue>` block already carries the issue's own facts and the When-to-act section interprets both buttons; the issue cases pass. In both, the fact already reaches the model through the channel it reads at that moment, so a note would say it twice. Nothing was added.

### Where each text lives

The architecture doc splits text the model reads between the Agent page (standing text, rendered the same every time) and C++ (text assembled from app state). The sentence about the picture is on the page in `fileReportInstructions.ts`, and the wider `view_render` description is in the registry: both are standing text. The file-open note and the `unchecked` sentence are built in C++ (`AgentHost::make_agent_request` and the coordinator's `intent_update` handler) because what they say depends on the moment: which presets are in force, whether a picture was rendered, whether a purpose is recorded.

### The standing prompt

The Preparing sentence "Inspect the project and set a printer, filament and process that suit it." became "Set a printer, filament and process that suit it." The inspection is now prompted where it applies: by the `unchecked` sentence the moment a purpose is recorded, and by the picture on the file-open turn. The prompt is 2,717 bytes, from 2,741; the pinned fixture was changed with it. No other prompt sentence was covered by the new texts, so none other was deleted. None of the new texts uses the words approve, authorize, or confirm before.

### C. The eval

- The deletion of `petg-restated` and `petg-restated-after-read` made in the main checkout (uncommitted there) was applied here identically, from a patch of that diff, as the branch's first commit. The main checkout's edits to the suite's README were part of that diff and are in the commit too.
- A new case, `after-intent`, starts at the request right after `intent_update` returned in the prepare conversation (a `record` on the `presets_list` reply in `script.json`). It passes on `settings_get`, `settings_search`, `presets_list` or `printer_setup_preview`, fails on `slice_start` or a reply the judge reads as claiming the print is ready, answers any other read, and leaves any other change unobserved. Three offline tests in `test_steps.py` cover those rules and that the recorded point ends with the `unchecked` sentence.
- The recorder (`--project-prompt-requests`) now checks, on the `file-note` conversation's opening turn, that the person's message ends with an image part and the request with the note. `requests.json` was re-recorded: 23 points, 3.79 MB.
- The `file-note-not-instructions` case does not carry the picture. Its point is the turn after the file opened ("ok what next?"), and the picture is deliberately not replayed into later turns, so no request in the recording holds it. The picture and note are verified on the opening turn by the recorder's checks and by the C++ tests instead. If a case should start at the opening turn itself, it needs a `record` on that reply and a case class.

**Proposed live batch (not run; needs Kenneth's approval).** Cases: `after-intent` (new), `prepare-petg-strong`, `after-preview`, `after-apply`, `after-slice` (the same conversation, now replaying the `unchecked` sentence in history), `file-note-not-instructions`, `print-this-no-purpose`. 3 runs each, 21 runs. At roughly 12k input tokens per request and up to 3 answered reads per run, about 650k input tokens (most cached), 15k output, up to 21 judge calls. A same-day before run of the same cases from the `jusprin-newui` checkout (its prompt and its recording) would double that. Credentials stay in `~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`.

## 3. Tests and results

Build: fresh worktree, configured with Release rather than RelWithDebInfo because the disk had 18 GiB free and a RelWithDebInfo tree costs about 14 GB; the code and tests are the same. Pages built with `jusprin_web` after the page edits, and the built bundle was checked for the new sentence and the trimmed one.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `agent_bridge_tests` | all 296 cases, 10,543 assertions pass. Before re-recording, 5 assertions failed: the old recording's `intent_update` results had no `unchecked`, as the new schema requires. |
| AgentUI vitest | 23 files, 415 tests pass |
| `workspace_contract_tests` | 42 cases, 320 assertions pass |
| Shell harness default scenario | PASS, 553 checks, 0 failures |
| Shell harness `--project-prompt-requests` | PASS, 7,338 checks, 0 failures; log shows `file-note opened turn: picture=1` and the note, and `recorded after-intent` |
| `python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py` | 16 tests OK |
| `run_prompt_tests.py --render-only` | 23 bodies render; 69 requests, 2,972,730 bytes |

New behaviour and the tests that fail without it: the bridge test asserts the picture and the exact note on the file-open request, their absence on the follow-up, the empty-plate and purpose-recorded variants; the adapter test asserts the image part is last in the user message and the developer note is the request's last item, and that a title request has neither; the coordinator test asserts the `unchecked` sentence with and without presets; the vitest file asserts the picture sentence and the two removed ones; the recorder's two new checks run against the real app; the fixture test pins the prompt bytes.

Line counts (excluding `requests.json`): app code and its C++ and page tests, 185 added, 10 removed; eval case, recorder check and the case deletion, 93 added, 49 removed. `requests.json`: 3,942 added, 7,403 removed, regenerated.

## 4. Remaining issues

- Nothing was measured against a live model; the batch above is the proposal.
- The note is a trailing developer item. The OpenAI Responses API accepts that; OpenRouter maps it to a system message for DeepSeek, which accepts system messages in any position. A provider that refuses a system message after a user message would fail the file-open turn. Not verified live.
- The picture's size per file-open turn was not measured (a 1024 by 768 PNG of a lit plate, base64). It is sent once per opened file and never replayed.
- The picture and note exist only for the file-open turn. A model imported later with `object_import_file`, or a project whose purpose is recorded, gets neither; the `view_render` description is what covers those.
- The `unchecked` sentence is replayed in history on every later request of that conversation, as every tool result is. It is about 200 bytes.
- The two intermediate commits are not individually green: at 17112e7e71 the runner's case list and the old recording disagree, and at 553916458f the old recording fails the schema check. The branch tip passes everything.
- The main checkout still has the case deletion uncommitted; its `requests.json` differs from this branch's new recording.
